title: Docs + SDK guidance for route-level quantization controls (opt-in Quantization Profile Library)
creator: Alex Martinez
description:
Background
Customers can opt in to quantization via route-level enablement controls (with canary + rollback). We need consistent developer-facing documentation (API + Console) and SDK guidance so customers can safely adopt and troubleshoot.

Scope
- Update Redwood docs to explain:
  1) what “quantization profiles” are (high level),
  2) how route-level enablement works (incl. canary),
  3) what to expect when a request falls back to baseline,
  4) troubleshooting for quality/format regressions (especially JSON / tool-calling routes).
- Update SDK docs/examples (Python + TS) for configuring route-level settings where applicable and for inspecting route/model execution status.
- Align terminology: “Quantization Profile”, “Baseline”, “Quantized execution”, “Fallback to baseline”. Avoid “preset/variant” in customer-facing docs.

Out of scope
- Writing full “quantization theory” content.
- User-supplied profiles (v1 is Redwood-published only).

Primary audiences
- App engineers using Hosted API routes (self-serve).
- Platform teams enabling quantization for background/batch workloads while keeping interactive chat baseline.

Implementation notes / decisions to document
- Route-level config is the supported control surface for enabling quantization. We should not document per-request override headers for v1 unless Product explicitly approves.
- Canary behavior: route can be set to 0–100% quantized. Remaining traffic stays baseline.
- Fallback behavior: if profile is incompatible with hardware/kernel/sequence-length regime (or temporarily unavailable), runtime falls back to baseline and emits metrics/tags.
- Safe adoption guidance: start with non-user-facing/background routes (summarization, offline enrichment), then expand.

Deliverables
1) Customer docs page(s)
- “Quantization Profiles (Beta)” overview and “Enable per route” guide.
- Console instructions (Route Settings → Quantization).
- API configuration instructions (route config endpoint / settings payload shape).
- Monitoring section: where to see quantized vs baseline execution, and what to watch.
- Rollback section: quick disable per route + expected propagation time.

2) SDK guidance
- Python: helper usage (if available) to update route settings; examples in README/snippets.
- TypeScript: types/fields so apps can introspect whether a route is running quantized vs baseline.

3) Troubleshooting section
- Quality regressions: how to canary, compare outputs, and disable.
- Output format regressions: JSON mode / tool-calling; recommended mitigation = disable quantization on that route.
- Performance regressions on long-context: how to check sequence-length regime notes and confirm fallback behavior.
- Common errors: permission/validation errors when writing route config; explain likely causes.

Acceptance criteria
- Docs page clearly shows the step-by-step enablement flow (Console + API).
- Docs explicitly call out: opt-in, route-scoped, canary supported, fast rollback.
- Troubleshooting includes at least 3 concrete scenarios:
  - JSON mode formatting regression
  - tool-calling schema adherence regression
  - perf regression on long context (or no expected speedup)
- SDK docs/examples compile and match the current API surface.
- Links to monitoring dashboards and rollback runbook included.

References
- Docs PR (draft): sources/github/redwood-docs/pr_1207_docs_quantization_profiles_route_enablement.json
- Python SDK PR: sources/github/redwood-sdk-python/pr_804_add_route_config_helpers_quantization.json
- TS SDK PR: sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr_655_add_types_for_quantization_profile_status.json
- API conventions: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/quantization-profile-config-api-conventions.json
- Design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/quantization-profile-library-route-controls-design-spec.json
- Rollback runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/quantization-profile-rollback-runbook.json

Open questions
- Do we want to document any per-request override (e.g., header to force baseline) for troubleshooting? Current plan: no (keep control plane as source of truth). If needed for support, document as internal-only.
- Should we expose “effective execution mode” in response metadata for customers by default, or only in Console/telemetry? Currently SDK PRs assume it’s available as a status field; confirm with Nikhil + Logan before GA.

Risks
- Docs may drift from actual field names/validation rules as route-settings API evolves. Mitigation: add a small contract test in docs build (or a snippet generator) once API stabilizes.

Checklist
- [ ] Confirm final naming in Console UI (Quantization section label + warnings)
- [ ] Confirm route settings endpoint + payload examples with Platform (Ethan / Jordan)
- [ ] Confirm telemetry tags and customer-visible fields with Telemetry (Logan / Nadia)
- [ ] Merge docs PR
- [ ] Merge SDK PRs
- [ ] Post release note snippet to Product (Aditya / Nikhil) for beta comms
